info.title: Maquettiste editor API
info.summary: The JSON API the Maquettiste editor's C# functions expose on the editor's own domain (SPEC Section 16), phase 2 subset.
info.description:
The editor site's `_functions/` answer this API on the editor's domain (`http://maquettiste.localhost:8080` in local
mode). Every handler is route parsing, the sign-in check and one call into `Maquettiste.Engine`
(`docs/engineering/engine-design.md` section 15, `docs/engineering/phase2-design.md` section 3). The binding
design is `docs/engineering/phase2-design.md`; this file is the contract the editor SPA, its generated client and its
MSW mocks are built from.

**Serialization.** Every body that mirrors an engine record is that record serialized by `System.Text.Json` with
`JsonSerializerDefaults.Web` and no custom converters (host-contracts requirement 5): camelCase names, every
property written, `null` included, enums as the kebab-case strings the engine declares, `TimeSpan` as
`[-][d.]hh:mm:ss[.fffffff]`, `DateTimeOffset` as ISO 8601 with offset, and non-ASCII and HTML-sensitive characters
escaped as `\uXXXX` (the default encoder). Computed public properties are serialized too (`ChangeSet.isEmpty`,
`ValidationReport.hasErrors`). Schemas marked `x-engine-record` name the C# record they mirror; a change to that
record is a change to this file in the same commit.

**Model documents.** Request bodies that carry an element, and `ElementDocument.json`, are canonical model files
as `schemas/v1/<kind>.json` defines them (canonical JSON omits defaults). `ElementDocument.element` is the same
element as the engine's typed record, with every property present (defaults and `null`s written). The editor edits
and sends `json`, never `element`.

**Hashes and ETags.** An element's hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of its canonical file bytes (64 characters,
no prefix). Responses carry it as a strong ETag (`ETag: "<hash>"`); `If-Match` accepts the quoted or bare hash.

**Authentication.** One middleware (`[Middleware(Order = 0)]`) gates every request to the site, static files
included. It admits, in order: (1) in local mode (`MAQUETTISTE_MODE=local`, the default) unless
`MAQUETTISTE_LOCAL_TRUST=off`, a request whose remote address, normalised from its IPv4-mapped form (Kestrel
listens dual-stack and reports `::ffff:172.17.0.1`), is loopback or one of `MAQUETTISTE_LOCAL_PEERS` (the
container's gateway, which is how a `127.0.0.1` port binding reaches the container), whose `Host` is
`localhost`, a `*.localhost` name, `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, and which carries no `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-For`,
`X-Forwarded-Host` or `X-Real-IP` header, signed in as the local admin with no credential; (2) `Authorization: Bearer
<MAQUETTISTE_EDITOR_TOKEN>` (the CLI and scripts); (3) the `mq_session` cookie set by `POST /api/session`. Phase 2
has one role in use, `admin`; each operation names the least role it will need once accounts land
(`x-maquettiste-role`). A state-changing request whose `Origin` header is present and is not the site's own origin
is refused with 403 `forbidden-origin`, and a `POST` or `PUT` body must be `application/json` (cross-site request
forgery defence for the credential-less local mode).

**Errors.** Outcomes of engine calls come back as engine records (`SaveResult`, `BatchResult`, `ValidationReport`,
`PreviewResult`, `JobInfo`) with the status the outcome maps to. Everything else (authentication, routing, bad
input, a full job queue, an unexpected failure) is an RFC 9457 problem document (`Problem`) with a stable `code`.

**Realtime.** Long work runs as jobs; progress and model changes arrive over the host's SignalR hub at
`/_host/realtime` (`site.realtime` from `/_host/site.js` in the browser), not over this API. The event payloads
are the `Realtime*` schemas under `components.schemas`; `x-maquettiste-realtime` at the root lists each event,
its group and its schema.

**Engine additions.** Operations and schemas marked `x-engine-addition` need an engine call that phase 1 does not
have (E1 to E4 in `phase2-design.md` section 3.8); their shapes are binding for that work.

x-maquettiste-realtime.notes:
The browser only listens and joins; the functions publish with IRealtime. Payloads are at most 256 KB of JSON:
model.changed and validation.completed are cut with ChangeSet.TruncateTo and ValidationReport.TruncateTo to 200 KB
and carry `truncated: true` when cut, and the editor then refetches (`GET /api/model/index`, `POST /api/validate`).
job.completed is a fixed-size summary (RealtimeJobCompleted), never the JobInfo, whose stale lists and diagnostics
can exceed the limit; the editor reads `GET /api/jobs/{id}` for the record.
[RealtimeConnect] admits the same callers as the middleware and returns their user name; [RealtimeJoin] admits a
signed-in connection to `editors` and to `job:{id}` for any job id (a ULID).
x-maquettiste-realtime.events: See `webhooks`. Each realtime event is described there as a webhook so client generators emit its payload type; nothing is POSTed, the hub delivers it.

post.summary: Store the project icon under .maquettiste/branding/
post.description:
The body is JSON, as every write of the API: `{ contentType, data }` with the file in base64. An SVG or a PNG of at most
512 KB; an SVG is stored without its scripts, event handlers, external references and processing instructions (listed in
`removed`). The file is written under a content-addressed name, `branding/icon-<12 hex>.svg` or `.png`, in the model
folder, so an upload never replaces the icon the saved settings name; `maquettiste.json` is not changed: save
`branding.icon` with the returned `icon` through `PUT /api/project/settings`. That save removes the uploaded icons the
settings no longer name.

get.summary: Summaries of every element
get.description:
One summary per top-level element (sub-elements such as attributes and relation ends are not listed). The explorer,
the command palette and every canvas start from this list.

E5e: the response carries an `ETag`, a hash of every row's id, file hash and path and of the index format, so it
changes exactly when a row does, across server restarts too. The index format constant is `maquettiste-index/e6`.

`?locale=<tag>` (a declared locale; the default locale is the same as none) fills `displayName` from that locale's fallback
chain (reference-types-seeds-localization.md section 3.8) from a per-locale display-name table the host builds once per
snapshot; the ETag then also covers the locale, its chain and the hashes of the chain's shards. 400 for an undeclared locale. A request whose `If-None-Match` names it gets 304 with no
body. `Cache-Control: no-cache` lets the browser keep the index and revalidate it on every use.

The index filters (`kind`, `package`, `tag`, `category`, `stereotype`, `query`; all optional, combined with AND) narrow the
list, as `getElements` and the MCP tool `get_model_index` take them. `limit` or `cursor` pages it: the body is then one page
of rows ordered by kind, name and id (ordinal), and while more rows follow, a `Link` header with `rel="next"` gives the URL of
the next page (the same query with `cursor` set). A filtered or paged answer carries no ETag and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
Use the index to find elements, `getElements` to read their documents in bulk, `getResolvedModel` for what generation sees,
and `getModelKinds` for the counts.

parameters.description: A declared locale whose display names fill `displayName`.

get.summary: The resolved model as flat records, in pages
get.description:
What templates read (the resolved model of SPEC Section 10), as data for external systems. Resolved objects reference each
other, so they are projected into flat records (`x-engine-record`) where other objects appear by id; each record has `id`,
`kind` and `name`. Choose what to read with `scope`, which follows the template scopes (`get_template_context`):

- `entities`: `EntityRecord`, each attribute resolved (`type` with the enum, value object, scalar or reference type it
  names, `default`, `length`, `precision`, `scale`, `isKey`; the base entity's attributes come first, marked `isInherited`),
  the key, alternate keys, `base` and `derived`, navigations, `relations`, one mapping per database (table key and the
  column of each attribute path) and the annotations.
- `relations`, `enums`, `value-objects`, `scalar-types`, `packages`, `reference-types` (with every row), `seeds`, `actors`,
  `scenarios`: the matching record.
- `processes`: `ProcessRecord`, every state at every depth with `parent` and `children`, the transitions, events, guards,
  actions, gates and invokes, actors by id.
- `databases`: `DatabaseRecord`, the database view of `getDatabaseView` (tables with columns, keys, foreign keys and
  indexes, views, sequences, routines, database types, SQL objects and queries); `tables`: one `TableRecord` per table,
  for databases too large for one record; `routines`, `database-types`, `sql-objects`, `queries`: one `RoutineRecord`,
  `DatabaseTypeRecord`, `SqlObjectRecord` or `QueryRecord` per object.
- `all` (the default): every scope but `tables`, `routines`, `database-types`, `sql-objects` and `queries`, which
  `databases` holds.

`database` narrows entities and relations to the ones mapped (not ignored) in that database, and databases and tables to
it; the other kinds are not narrowed. Records come ordered by kind, name and id (ordinal); pass `next` as `cursor` until it
is null. The model is validated and resolved once per model version, so paging through it costs one resolution; a change
between pages is tolerated (the next page starts after the last record read, in the changed model). A model with errors
returns no records and the errors in `diagnostics`. The MCP tool `get_resolved_model` and `maquettiste model export
--resolved` answer the same.

parameters.description: What to read.

parameters.description: A database id; only what is mapped to it.

get.summary: Element documents in pages
get.description:
The bulk document read for external systems: the canonical documents (as `getElement` returns them in `json`) of the
elements `ids` names, or of every element, narrowed by the index filters, in pages of `limit` (default 100, at most 1000),
ordered by kind, name and id (ordinal). Pass `next` as `cursor` until it is null. A cursor encodes the last position read,
so a change between pages is tolerated: the next page starts after that position in the current model (an element renamed
meanwhile may move before or after it).

`fields=name,attributes` keeps only those top-level members of each document (`id` and `kind` are always kept), so a
caller that needs names and attributes of thousands of entities reads only those. `ids` takes element or sub-element ids
(a sub-element id reads the element that holds it), at most 1000; ids that match nothing are listed in `missing`. The MCP
tool `get_elements` and `maquettiste model export` answer the same.

delete.description:
Refused while other elements reference it unless `resolution` says otherwise. `remove-references` clears optional
references; a required one makes the delete `invalid`, and the first diagnostic is the readable MQ2001 naming the referrer.
`delete-dependents` also resolves required references in the same change: the referrer loses the smallest part that is
valid without the reference (an attribute whose type is deleted, a diagram member, a key, a foreign key), or, when only
the whole referrer would do (a table, view, sequence or mapping of a deleted database; a relation, mapping or overlay of a
deleted entity), it is deleted with its own dependents, recursively. A deleted database's `databases.<name>` conventions
entry in `maquettiste.json` goes in the same change. `GET /api/model/elements/{id}/delete-plan` shows all of it first.

post.summary: Atomic multi-element change

is checked, and every file is staged and renamed into place; on any failure nothing is written. Failed items carry
their outcome; the other items report `saved` with no hash.

get.summary: The SQL of one query for a dialect
get.description:
Renders a query (a query element over a database's tables and views) as parameterised SQL for its database's dialect, or
the one named: the query's statement and one statement per collection. Identifiers are quoted by the database's quoting
setting, functions spelled per dialect, `ilike` lowered where the dialect has none, paging written as `LIMIT/OFFSET` or
`OFFSET … FETCH NEXT`. A collection runs once for all parent rows (a second round trip): the parent's statement carries
the correlation columns, the collection's takes their values as the list parameter `__keys0` (`__keys1`...) and returns
each row's as `__key0`. An `sql` expression without a text for the dialect is MQ4029 in `diagnostics`. A model with
errors returns `preview: null` and the diagnostics. The MCP tool `preview_query_sql` answers the same.

parameters.name: dialect
parameters.description: postgresql, sqlserver, mysql, sqlite or oracle; absent for the query's database's.

parameters.name: placeholder
parameters.description: The placeholder style, `@name` (default), `:name` or `$1`.

parameters.name: lists
parameters.description: How a list parameter is written, `IN @name` for a data access library that expands lists (default) or `= ANY(@name)` on PostgreSQL.

get.summary: The resolved tables of one database
get.description:
The physical model after conventions, mappings and table overlays are applied: every table (synthesized,
designed or imported), its columns with the attribute each one stores, keys, foreign keys and indexes, and
every view, sequence, routine, database type, SQL object, query and schema. The database, each schema, table, column,
view, sequence, routine, database type, SQL object and query carries the annotations of its own file or entry (display and plural names, description, stereotypes, tags, category,
properties, generation hints); a synthesized table without an overlay, or a synthesized column without an
overlay entry, has none. The Database workspace draws table diagrams from it and the Mappings workspace
sets it beside the entity. A model with errors returns `view: null` and the diagnostics.

200.description: The view, or the diagnostics that prevented resolution.

get.summary: The table list of one database, without columns
get.description:
E5c: a projection of the resolved database for the explorer's Databases and Mappings sections, table-name search and
the coverage line: every table's key, name, schema, origin, entity or relation and column count, without the columns.
Unlike `/view` it answers on a model with errors: the tables whose owning elements are valid come back, the rest are
left out, `partial` is true and the diagnostics say why. The editor keeps the last complete list per database and
shows it with a stale badge while a response is partial. Per model version the server validates the model once and
resolves each database asked for on its own (the conceptual layer and that database), so a change costs one database's
resolve; `diagnostics` then holds the validation diagnostics and that database's resolution diagnostics.

200.description: The tables that resolve, the diagnostics, and whether the list is partial.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The table's key, as `TableSummary.key` (a table file's id, or a synthesized key such as `<entityId>@<databaseId>`).

get.summary: One table of a database with its columns, keys and indexes
get.description:
E5f: one `TableView` (columns with `attributeId`, primary key, foreign keys, unique constraints, indexes) for a table's
children in the explorer and column-level "mapped by", without `/view`'s every table. A projection of the same
per-version resolve as `/tables`: after the first call for a database and model version, a lookup. Like `/tables` it
answers on a model with errors; `table` is null when no table of the database has the key or when the table is left
out because an owning element has errors (`partial` then says so).

200.description: The table (or null), the diagnostics, and whether the model has errors.

get.summary: Localization settings and completeness per locale and shard
get.description:
reference-types-seeds-localization.md section 3.9. The default locale, the declared locales, and per translated locale its
fallback chain and per shard the expected, translated, missing and stale counts. A project without `localization` answers
`defaultLocale: null` and no locales.

200.description: The settings and the completeness counts.

get.summary: Translation entries of one locale, by owner, by shard or the missing ones
get.description:
reference-types-seeds-localization.md section 3.9. `?owner=<id>` or `?shard=<path>` returns entries with their source text,
translation, effective text, state, shard path and hash; with neither, every entry of the locale. `?missing=true&cursor=` pages
(200 per page) the entries that need work (`missing`, `fallback` or `stale`) for the translation queue; `cursor` is the
previous page's last `id/field`. 404 for a locale that is not declared or is the default.

200.description: The entries, and the cursor of the next page when paged.

put.summary: Write, remove or confirm translations of one locale
put.description:
reference-types-seeds-localization.md section 3.9. `{ entries: [{ id, field, value | null, confirm? }], expected: { shardPath:
hash } }`, one atomic save: 200 with the new hashes of the shards written, 409 when a shard named in `expected` changed (its
current hash in `hashes`, nothing written), 422 with diagnostics (MQ7202, MQ7203, MQ7211). `confirm` rewrites that field's
`src` hash without changing the text. Each entry goes to its node's shard; an entry held in another shard moves there.

200.description: The shards written and their new hashes.

409.description: A shard named in `expected` changed; `hashes` holds its current hash and nothing was written.

422.description: The entries are invalid; `diagnostics` says why and nothing was written.

get.summary: Export one locale as XLIFF 2.1 or CSV
get.description:
reference-types-seeds-localization.md section 3.9. `?format=xliff|csv&shard=`: XLIFF 2.1 with one `file` per shard and one
unit per field keyed `id/field` (segment `state` `translated` or `initial`, `subState` `maquettiste:<state>`), or CSV with the
columns `id, field, source, translation, state, shard`.

post.summary: Preview or apply an XLIFF or CSV translation import
post.description:
reference-types-seeds-localization.md section 3.9. `?dryRun=true` (the default) previews; `dryRun=false` writes the
translations as one save checked against the shard hashes read for the preview (409 when one changed). A unit with an empty
target is left alone; a unit naming no translatable field is ignored with MQ7203 in `diagnostics`.

200.description: The preview (or the result) of the import.

409.description: What the preview read changed before the import was applied; nothing was written.

422.description: The import makes the model invalid; `diagnostics` says why and nothing was written.

get.summary: Export a seed's rows as CSV
get.description:
reference-types-seeds-localization.md sections 2.3 and 3.9. RFC 4180, UTF-8, `@id` first, then `@code`, `@label` and `@description` for reference types, then attribute and end
role names in the seed's column order, then `@label:<locale>` and `@description:<locale>` per `locale`; `?bom=true` adds a
byte order mark and CRLF line ends. Reference cells export codes, collections `;`-joined codes, end cells row ids, value
objects compact JSON.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: Adds `@label:<locale>` and `@description:<locale>` columns; repeatable.

post.summary: Preview or apply a CSV import into a seed
post.description:
reference-types-seeds-localization.md sections 2.3 and 3.9. The body is JSON (`{ content }`, the CSV text), as every write
of the API. Rows match by `@id`, else by `@code` for reference types, else are new rows with new ids; `merge` updates and
adds, `replace` also removes rows missing from the file, except rows that cells of other seeds name (listed in `blocked`).
Headers that match no column are listed in `ignoredHeaders`. `?dryRun=true` (the default) previews; applying saves the seed
with `If-Match` (or the hash read for the preview; 409 when it changed, 422 with diagnostics) and then writes the
`@label:<locale>` and `@description:<locale>` translations.

200.description: The preview (or the result) of the import.

409.description: What the preview read changed before the import was applied; nothing was written.

422.description: The import makes the model invalid; `diagnostics` says why and nothing was written.

post.summary: Preview or apply CSV imports into several seeds (rows in one change, then translations)
post.description:
The editor's Import seed data…: one CSV per seed, each read as `POST /api/seeds/{id}/csv` reads one. `?dryRun=true`
(the default) previews every file; applying saves every changed seed in one all-or-nothing change (a stale `hash` or a
new error in any seed writes none: 409 or 422 with the diagnostics on the file concerned), then writes the files'
`@label:<locale>` and `@description:<locale>` translations. Two files for one seed are a 400.

hash.description: The seed hash read for the preview; the current one when absent.

200.description: One preview (or result) per file, in request order.

409.description: A seed changed since its preview; nothing was written.

422.description: The imports make the model invalid; the file concerned carries the diagnostics and nothing was written.

get.summary: The attributes that use a reference type, with their effective storage
get.description:
reference-types-seeds-localization.md section 3.9. Every attribute typed by the reference type, with its owner, domain, collection, required and the effective storage
choice per database.

post.summary: Simulate a process (or an unsaved draft of it) through a list of inputs
post.description:
phase-3-design.md sections 4.1 and 4.4. Simulation state lives in the client: every call replays `start` and `steps` from
the initial entry, so one input list always gives one trace, and two windows never diverge. `document` simulates an unsaved
draft of the process, checked as a save would check it (422 with the diagnostics when it adds an error). `scenario` runs a
scenario's start and steps first (the request's `start` is then ignored) and `steps` after them. The replay stops after an
input whose trace is incomplete (a guard with neither expression nor `assume`, MQ9305, MQ9507). `trace` starts at index
`from` (-1, the default, is the initial entry).

200.description: The traces and where the process stands after the last input.

422.description: The draft `document` adds an error; nothing ran.

post.summary: Record a scenario from a list of inputs
post.description:
phase-3-design.md section 4.4. The engine replays `start` and `steps` and fills each step's `expect` (refusals recorded as
`accepted: false`) and the `outcome` (unless the request gives one) from the replay, gives the scenario and its steps new ids,
and saves it as one change under `model/scenarios/<process file stem>/`. `?dryRun=true` returns the scenario without writing
it. Inputs that cannot be replayed to the last step (MQ9305, MQ9306, MQ9507) are 422 with the diagnostics.

200.description: The scenario a dry run would save.

201.description: The scenario was saved; `ETag` is its hash and `Location` its element.

409.description: The model changed while the scenario was saved; nothing was written.

422.description: The inputs cannot be replayed to the last step, or the scenario does not validate; nothing was written.

post.summary: Replay a process's scenarios and report each one's first failure
post.description:
phase-3-design.md sections 3 and 4.4. Every scenario of the process (or the ids or names in `scenarios`) is replayed through
the engine interpreter; `failure` is the first failed expectation (MQ9301 to MQ9304) or the stop that kept the replay from the
last step (MQ9305, MQ9306, MQ9507; `expected` and `actual` are then null). Results are ordered by name, then id.

get.summary: Export a process as an XState machine config
get.description:
phase-3-design.md section 5.1. The config in canonical key order (two-space indent, `\n` line ends, a trailing newline); what
has no XState home travels under `meta.maquettiste`, so importing the export over the process gives the same file.
`X-Maquettiste-Diagnostics` counts the MQ9406 notes (what went into `meta`); `X-Maquettiste-Warnings` counts the other
diagnostics (MQ9404: a kept opaque pointer that has no place in the config and was dropped). The CLI prints those to stderr
and the MCP tool returns every diagnostic in a second content block.

X-Maquettiste-Warnings.description: The number of other export diagnostics (MQ9404).

post.summary: Preview or apply an XState machine config import
post.description:
phase-3-design.md sections 5.1 and 5.2. `?dryRun=true` (the default) returns the process document the import gives with its
diagnostics (MQ9401 to MQ9406) and the ids it creates, writing nothing. `into` re-imports over an existing process (id or
name), keeping the ids of the nodes it matches; `removed` lists what it drops. With `dryRun=false` the document is saved as
one change: 409 when `into` changed since `expectedHash`, 422 when the import has errors or the process does not validate.

200.description: The preview, or the saved import (`applied` true, `hash`).

409.description: `into` changed since `expectedHash`; nothing was written.

422.description: The import has errors, or the process does not validate; nothing was written.

post.summary: Sync a lifecycle's bound enum with its root-level states
post.description:
phase-3-design.md sections 3 and 4.4, the `sync-enum` batch operation. The bound enum's members become the root-level states in
document order (ids, codes and descriptions kept). `dryRun: true` returns the plan. A member still used by a default,
`allowedValues`, a seed cell or a scenario value is listed in `refused` and not removed: there is no force flag, change the uses
first (applying such a plan is 422 with MQ9019). 409 when the process changed since `expectedHash`.

409.description: The process changed since `expectedHash`; nothing was written.

422.description: The process is not a bound lifecycle, or a removal is refused (MQ9019 in `diagnostics`); nothing was written.

post.summary: Start a dry run as a job
post.description:
Queues a plan job and returns it at once. Join the realtime group `job:{id}` for `job.progress` and
`job.completed`, then read `GET /api/jobs/{id}` once, so an event sent before the join is not missed. The
functions force `includeDiffs: false`, `stageBarriers: false` and `lock: wait`; `mode` is ignored (a plan is
always a dry run).

get.summary: The finished plan
get.description: Files added, changed and deleted, hand edits and conflicts (`changes`), per pack and unit. `units` (every unit's read keys and outputs) is large and empty unless `units=true`. The 20 newest plans are kept.

billing.summary: The billing fixture's first plan (units and changes trimmed in this example)

get.summary: Unified diff for one file in a plan
get.description: From the file on disk now to the planned bytes, without rendering again. Empty for a file the plan leaves unchanged or keeps; a deleted file diffs to nothing.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: A repo-relative path from the plan's `changes` or `units[].outputs`.

200.description: The unified diff (`--- a/`, `+++ b/`, hunks).

text/x-diff.example:
--- a/db/main/billing/tables/customers.sql
+++ b/db/main/billing/tables/customers.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@
+-- Generated by Maquettiste (sql-ddl/table). Do not edit; changes are overwritten.
+-- Table billing.customers of database main (PostgreSQL 16).
+-- Maps entity Customer.
+
+CREATE TABLE billing.customers (
+    id uuid NOT NULL,
+    name varchar(120) NOT NULL,
+    email varchar(254) NOT NULL,
+    customer_since date NULL,
+    created_at timestamptz(6) NOT NULL,
+    updated_at timestamptz(6) NULL,
+    CONSTRAINT pk_customers PRIMARY KEY (id),
+    CONSTRAINT uq_customers_email UNIQUE (email)
+);

post.summary: Apply a plan by id as a job
post.description: The job's `applyResult.outcome` is `stale` (with `staleUnits` and `stalePaths`, nothing written) when any input or planned path changed since planning, `failed` when the plan is unknown or its stored bytes are gone, `invalid` when the plan or the model now has errors. Only `failed` (and `cancelled`) change the job's `state`; a `stale`, `invalid` or `conflicts` apply is a job in state `succeeded`, so check `applyResult.outcome`.

get.summary: Queued, running and recent jobs, newest first
get.description: Run history and the queue. Finished jobs keep no per-file or per-unit lists (read the plan for those).

get.summary: Job state, progress, result or error

running.summary: A plan job while it validates

applied.summary: A finished apply job (changes trimmed in this example)

delete.summary: Cancel a queued or running job
delete.description: A queued job is removed and recorded `cancelled` at once; a running one stops within one second and its `job.completed` follows.

post.summary: Render one unit against one element, with no writes
post.description:
The Database workspace's DDL preview calls `sql-ddl`/`table` with a resolved table key (`<entityId>@<databaseId>`
for a synthesized entity table, a table file's id for a designed one) and `sql-ddl`/`schema` with a database id.
The unit renders even when its `where` filter would not plan it. A model with errors returns the errors and no
files. An element outside the unit's scope (another kind than its `each`, one its selector does not return, an
element for a `model` unit, or none for an element unit) returns MQ6026 and no files, before anything renders
(pointer `/units/<i>/for` of the pack's `pack.json`).
With `unitOverride`, `overlay` or `parameters` the unit renders with unsaved text (generation-ui.md section 5.2): the
pack loads even when disabled, the sandbox limits apply and the render has a deadline of `limits.scriptTimeoutMs` x 4
(MQ6007 when it is hit). Unsaved text is code the server runs, so such a request needs the maintainer role (403 below
it). Nothing is written.

parameters.name: X-Maquettiste-Client
parameters.description:
The caller's live-preview key (any opaque string, e.g. per editor tab). A newer request of this kind with the same
value cancels one still in flight on the server (409 `superseded`); without it nothing is superseded.

files.text:
-- Generated by Maquettiste (sql-ddl/table). Do not edit; changes are overwritten.
-- Table billing.customers of database main (PostgreSQL 16).
-- Maps entity Customer.

CREATE TABLE billing.customers (
    id uuid NOT NULL,
    name varchar(120) NOT NULL,
    email varchar(254) NOT NULL,
    customer_since date NULL,
    created_at timestamptz(6) NOT NULL,
    updated_at timestamptz(6) NULL,
    CONSTRAINT pk_customers PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT uq_customers_email UNIQUE (email)
);

wrongElement.summary: A table unit asked for an entity id

diagnostics.message: The variable or function `table` was not found

outOfScope.summary: An entity unit asked for a reference type

diagnostics.message: This template expects an entity (unit 'entity' is 'each entity'), not 'Currency' (reference-type); pick one.

409.description:
`superseded`: a newer request of this kind with the same `X-Maquettiste-Client` cancelled this one on the server
(one request of each kind is in flight per client key, generation-ui.md section 5.2).

post.summary: A unit's rendered output paths over its scope, with the count, collisions and root checks
post.description:
Plans the unit as the planner does (its scope, then `generation.skip` hints, then its filter), or keeps only
`elementIds`, and renders each planned element up to `limit` (default 200, at most 2000) to report its output paths.
`count` is the whole scope. Diagnostics carry MQ6019 (the pattern cannot stay under an allowed root), MQ6020 (two
elements of the unit render the same path), MQ6005 (paths that differ only by case), MQ6004 per refused path, and
MQ6007 when the deadline (`limits.scriptTimeoutMs` x 4) is hit. With `unitOverride`, `overlay` or `parameters` it
renders unsaved text, which needs the maintainer role (403 below it). Nothing is written.

parameters.name: X-Maquettiste-Client
parameters.description:
The caller's live-preview key (any opaque string, e.g. per editor tab). A newer request of this kind with the same
value cancels one still in flight on the server (409 `superseded`); without it nothing is superseded.

409.description:
`superseded`: a newer request of this kind with the same `X-Maquettiste-Client` cancelled this one on the server
(one request of each kind is in flight per client key, generation-ui.md section 5.2).

get.summary: Completion data for a unit's templates
get.description: The globals a template of the unit sees (with `pack.params.*`), the members of the model and of the scope's records in snake_case, and the built-in helpers.

get.summary: Every pack with its units and load diagnostics
get.description: Every folder under `templates/` with a `pack.json`, enabled or not, in ordinal order. A pack whose `pack.json` does not load has `version` null, no units and its diagnostics.

post.summary: Create a pack from empty or from a pack of this project
post.description: `from` is `empty` (one `each entity` unit and its template) or the name of a pack of this project, whose files are copied with the new name in `pack.json`. `pack.json` is written in canonical form. 409 when the folder exists.

201.description: Created; `files` lists what was written and `hash` is the new `pack.json` hash.

409.description: The pack folder exists.

422.description: The starter is unknown; nothing was written.

get.summary: pack.json with its ETag, parameters, files and diagnostics
get.description:
`document` is `pack.json` as written (every member, `null` when it is not JSON). `parameters` joins the defaults, the
`parameterSchema` properties and the project values of `packs.<pack>.parameters`. `files` lists the folder with sizes,
hashes (each file's ETag), roles and users. `diagnostics` holds the load diagnostics (MQ6001, MQ6002, MQ6021 to MQ6024),
MQ6019 for output paths outside every root and MQ6003 / MQ6025 for templates that do not parse.

put.summary: Save the whole pack.json document in canonical form
put.description: Every member is kept (`version`, `description`, `engine`, `scripts`, `usesSchemaDiff`, `units`, `parameters`, `parameterSchema`). A schema failure (MQ6001, MQ6021) or a `name` that is not the folder is 422 and writes nothing; unit problems (MQ6019, MQ6022) are saved and reported in `diagnostics`.

409.description: pack.json changed since it was read; `hash` and `current` are the disk version.

422.description: The document is invalid; nothing was written.

delete.summary: Remove a pack, leaving the files it generated on disk
delete.description:
`If-Match` carries the `pack.json` hash read. Removes the `packs.<pack>` entry of `maquettiste.json` (through the settings
save), then the folder `.maquettiste/templates/<pack>/`, then the pack's committed and built manifests and its unit states.
The files the pack generated stay on disk and are no longer tracked: `untracked` lists them. Waits for a generation run in
progress. 409 when `pack.json` changed (or `maquettiste.json` kept changing meanwhile); 422 (nothing removed) when the settings save is refused. Sends `project.changed`
when the settings changed, then `templates.changed` (empty `files`) and `packs.changed`.

409.description: pack.json changed since it was read; `hash` and `current` are the disk version.

422.description: The settings save was refused; nothing was removed.

post.summary: Rename a pack, keeping the files it generated tracked
post.description:
`If-Match` carries the `pack.json` hash read. The new name follows the pack-name rule (lowercase letters and digits separated
by single hyphens, starting with a letter) and must not be used by another pack folder, a `packs.<name>` settings entry or
the manifests of a former pack. Moves the `packs.<pack>` entry of `maquettiste.json` to `packs.<name>` with its values
(through the settings save), renames the folder `.maquettiste/templates/<pack>/` (never a copy), writes the new name into
`pack.json`, and moves the pack's committed and built manifests and its unit states, so the files it generated stay tracked
and no later run deletes them as orphans. Generation hints keyed by the old name are listed in `hints` and left as they are:
the editor moves them with one model batch after the rename, so they are one undo step.
With `dryRun` every check runs and the answer says what would move, writing nothing. Waits for a generation run in
progress. 409 when `pack.json` changed (or `maquettiste.json` kept changing meanwhile); 422 (nothing changed) when the
name is refused or the settings save is. Sends `project.changed` when the settings changed, then
`templates.changed` (empty `files`) for both names and `packs.changed`. The ETag is the new `pack.json` hash.

409.description: pack.json changed since it was read; `hash` and `current` are the disk version.

422.description: The new name is not a pack name, is the current one, or is taken, or the settings save was refused; nothing changed.

get.summary: One pack file's text with its ETag

put.description:
`If-Match` with the hash read, or `If-None-Match: *` to create. The text must be UTF-8 with no NUL, at most 1 MB. A template
that fails to parse is saved and its MQ6003 diagnostics returned (GU6). `path=pack.json` is 400: `pack.json` is saved whole
through `PUT /api/packs/{pack}`. A path that leaves the pack folder, lexically or through a link, is 400.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The hash read; required unless `If-None-Match` is `*`.

409.description: The file changed since it was read (or exists, on create); `hash` and `current` are the disk version.

422.description: Not text, or larger than 1 MB; nothing was written.

delete.description: Refused (409, `referenced`) while a unit names the file or a template includes it; `diagnostics` says which.

409.description: The file changed since it was read, or something uses it.

post.summary: Move one pack file, optionally rewriting the units that name it
post.description:
`If-Match` carries the source file's hash. The target must not exist. With `updateUnits` the unit templates, companion
templates and scripts of `pack.json` that name `from` are rewritten (canonical) in the same write, and
`expectedPackHash` (the `pack.json` hash read) is required. 409 when either hash is stale, or (`referenced`) while a
template includes `from`, or while a unit names it and `updateUnits` is not set.

200.description: Moved; the ETag is the moved file's hash.

409.description: A hash is stale, or something includes or names the file.

422.description: The target exists, or `expectedPackHash` is missing with `updateUnits`.

get.summary: The custom property schemas and script rules of the model
get.description:
The files of `.maquettiste/extensions/`: the extension schemas (`<name>.json`, custom properties) first, then the script rules
(`rules/<name>.js`), each ordinal by path, with size, hash and what is wrong with the file on its own: an invalid schema
(MQ5004) or a rule script that does not load alone in the sandbox (MQ5002 for a syntax error or a registration without an
id, MQ5003 for a limit), with line and column. Rule findings (`x/<id>`) come from `POST /api/validate`.

get.summary: One extension file's text with its ETag

put.description:
`If-Match` with the hash read, or `If-None-Match: *` to create. The text must be UTF-8 with no NUL, at most 1 MB, and the
write goes through the engine's model write guard. A schema must be JSON that passes `extension.json`, else 422 with its
MQ5004 diagnostics and nothing written; it is written in canonical form and `text` returns what was written. A rule script is
written as sent, then loaded alone in the sandbox: a syntax error or a registration without an id comes back at once in
`diagnostics` (MQ5002 with line and column). The model is refreshed before the answer, `project.changed` is published and a
validation follows, so the rule's `x/<id>` findings reach the Problems panel. A path other than `<name>.json` or
`rules/<name>.js`, or one through a link, is 400.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The hash read; required unless `If-None-Match` is `*`.

409.description: The file changed since it was read (or exists, on create); `hash` and `current` are the disk version.

422.description: Not text, larger than 1 MB, or a schema that is not valid; nothing was written.

409.description: The file changed since it was read.

post.summary: Rename one extension file within its kind
post.description:
`If-Match` carries the source file's hash. The target must not exist and must be of the same kind (a schema stays a
`<name>.json`, a rule a `rules/<name>.js`), else 422. Nothing refers to an extension file by its path, so nothing else changes.

200.description: Moved; the ETag is the moved file's hash.

409.description: The source changed since it was read.

422.description: The target exists or is of another kind.

get.summary: The files a pack's manifests record
get.description: Every manifest entry of the pack (committed and built roots) with its unit, element, root, mode and state on disk (`intact`, `edited`, `missing`), and when a manifest was last written.

get.summary: One unit of a plan with its reason, causes and grouped read keys
get.description: "Why not" for a skipped unit (generation-ui.md section 4.3): its recorded read keys grouped by cause kind and a one-sentence summary. The unit key travels as the `key` query parameter since it holds `/` and `:`.

post.summary: Why a unit does or does not render an element
post.description:
The first reason that applies (generation-ui.md section 4.3): `pack-invalid`, `unknown-unit`, `pack-disabled`,
`unknown-element`, `scope`, `selector`, `skip-hint`, `filter`; or, when the unit plans the element, the plan's reason
and causes, from `planId` when that plan holds the unit, else from a new dry-run plan of the pack (which is stored like
any plan and named by `planId` in the answer). Works for elements no plan contains.

put.description: Stores the selection of one realtime connection that belongs to the caller and publishes `presence.changed` to `editors`. Idempotent; the editor sends it when the selection or workspace changes (debounced 250 ms) and after every reconnect.

post.summary: Realtime event `model.changed` (group: (all))
post.description: Delivered over the host hub `/_host/realtime`, not as an HTTP request. Sent after every save, create, delete or batch, and after the file watcher or the periodic rescan indexes a change on disk.

200.description: Not applicable; realtime events have no response.

post.summary: Realtime event `validation.completed` (group: (all))
post.description: Delivered over the host hub `/_host/realtime`, not as an HTTP request. Sent after a whole-model validation that follows one or more model.changed or project.changed events (debounced 750 ms).

200.description: Not applicable; realtime events have no response.

post.summary: Realtime event `project.changed` (group: (all))
post.description: Delivered over the host hub `/_host/realtime`, not as an HTTP request. Sent when maquettiste.json, a pack or an extension schema changed (a settings save or a disk change); a validation.completed follows.

200.description: Not applicable; realtime events have no response.

post.summary: Realtime event `templates.changed` (group: (all))
post.description: Delivered over the host hub `/_host/realtime`, not as an HTTP request. Sent once per pack whose files changed, beside project.changed (never instead of it), by the watcher and by the pack writes of this API; packs.changed follows.

200.description: Not applicable; realtime events have no response.

post.summary: Realtime event `packs.changed` (group: (all))
post.description: Delivered over the host hub `/_host/realtime`, not as an HTTP request. Names the packs of the templates.changed events just sent.

200.description: Not applicable; realtime events have no response.

post.summary: Realtime event `job.progress` (group: job:{id})
post.description: Delivered over the host hub `/_host/realtime`, not as an HTTP request. Sent while a job runs, at most four per second per job.

200.description: Not applicable; realtime events have no response.

post.summary: Realtime event `job.completed` (group: job:{id})
post.description: Delivered over the host hub `/_host/realtime`, not as an HTTP request. Sent once, when a job finishes (state `succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`). A bounded summary: read `GET /api/jobs/{id}` for the record. Report the run by `outcome`, not `state`.

200.description: Not applicable; realtime events have no response.

post.summary: Realtime event `presence.changed` (group: editors)
post.description: Delivered over the host hub `/_host/realtime`, not as an HTTP request. Sent a window reports its selection (PUT /api/presence), or a connection of the editors group goes away.

200.description: Not applicable; realtime events have no response.

post.summary: Realtime event `site.deployed` (group: (all, sent by the host))
post.description: Delivered over the host hub `/_host/realtime`, not as an HTTP request. Sent a deploy, rollback or functions upload of the editor site went live; the editor reloads itself.

BatchOp.description: `translate` (reference-types-seeds-localization.md section 3.9) is declared; until its handler lands a batch that holds one is refused with MQ1002 at `/operations/<n>/op`. The schema operations (erratum E26) act on database `id`: `add-schema` (`name`, optional `schema` id), `rename-schema` (`schema`, `name`; the default follows the rename), `remove-schema` (`schema`; refused with MQ4015 listing what lives there unless `target` names the schema it moves to, and refused for the default unless `default` names the new default) and `set-default-schema` (`schema`). Each expands into updates of the database and of the tables, views, sequences and mappings it moves; `items` then holds the other operations' results followed by one per element the schema operations changed. The process operations (phase-3-design.md sections 3 and 4.4): `sync-enum` (`id` a lifecycle process; its bound enum's members become the bound states in document order, keeping the ids, codes and descriptions of kept members; refused with MQ9019 when a removed member is still used by a default, allowed values, a seed cell or a scenario value, or when another operation of the batch writes the process or the enum), `set-lifecycle` (`id` an entity, `target` a process: binds both sides in one change and unbinds the previous partners; without `target` it clears the entity's lifecycle and turns the bound process back into an orchestration), `set-initial` (`id` a process or a compound state, `target` one of its direct children) and `refresh-scenario` (`id` a scenario: every step's `expect` and the `outcome` are rewritten from a replay in the engine interpreter; refused when the replay cannot reach the last step, or when another operation of the batch writes the scenario or its process). They expand into updates the same way, and a refusal is MQ9019 at `/operations/<n>`.

QueryView.description:
One resolved query (a query over the database's tables and views, written as data), with the annotations of its file (as
`TableView`). The trees (`where`, `having`, `groupBy`, `orderBy`, each field's `expression`, a join's `on`, a collection's
`query`) are as the file writes them (`query.json`); resolution adds the sources' tables and views, each field's type,
the collections' correlation keys and the SQL for the database's dialect.

entityId.description: The entity each result row has, or null for an ad hoc row (the select list).

sql.description: The SQL for the database's dialect with `@name` placeholders, with the hidden key columns its collections need.

sqlParameters.description: The parameters the SQL names, in first-appearance order.

uses.description: The ids (a synthesized table's key) of the tables, views, routines and database types the query reads.

type.description: The built-in type keyword, or null when a database type gives the type.

codeType.description: The built-in keyword a code type map maps (a database type's base, or string).

collection.description: Whether the caller passes a list of values.

QuerySourceView.description: A source of a query, the first (`kind` from) or a joined one.

source.description: The source as the file writes it (a table or view id, a table key or an entity id).

QueryFieldView.description: A field of a select list, with its inferred type.

QueryCollectionView.description: A collection of a query, its nested query and the statement that fills it for every parent row at once.

attribute.description: The file's attribute (an attribute id, a relation end id or an ad hoc name).

QueryKeyView.description:
A correlation key of a collection: the parent row carries the value as `parentField` (a hidden column when no select field
does), the collection's statement takes the parent values as the list parameter `parameter` and returns each row's value as
`childField`.

QuerySqlPreview.description: The SQL of one query for one dialect.

parameters.description: The parameters the statement names, in first-appearance order (the positions of `$n` placeholders).

example.name: InvoicesByCustomer
example.sql:
SELECT i.id AS id, i.number AS number
FROM billing.invoices i
WHERE i.customer_id = @customerId
ORDER BY i.issued_on DESC
LIMIT @limit OFFSET @offset

collections.name: lines
collections.sql:
SELECT l.id AS id, l.quantity AS quantity, l.invoice_id AS __key0
FROM billing.invoice_lines l
WHERE l.invoice_id IN @__keys0

default.description: The literal default as a plain JSON value, or null.

sequenceId.description: The id of the sequence that supplies values (a sequence file's id, or a synthesized key such as `<entityId>.sequence@<databaseId>`).

dbTypeId.description: The id of the database type the column uses (its file's `nativeType` names the type by id or name), or null. Always sent by this engine; optional for older servers.

displayName.description: The display name the column's own entry sets, or null; there is no fallback.

pluralName.description: The plural name the column's own entry sets, or null; there is no fallback.

stereotypes.description: The stereotype keys, in application order.

category.description: The id of the category-tree node.

properties.description: The custom properties, the stereotypes' default properties merged under the entry's own.

generation.description: The generation hints by pack name or `*`.

JobState.description: Where the job is in its life, not whether the run did what was asked. `succeeded` means the run completed and produced a result, whatever its outcome (`JobQueue` maps only the `cancelled` and `failed` run outcomes to other states), so a `stale`, `invalid`, `conflicts`, `drift` or `busy` run is `succeeded` too. The run's result is `planResult.outcome` or `applyResult.outcome`.

JobInfo.description: A finished job read back keeps no per-file or per-unit list (`planResult.plan.units` and `.changes`, `applyResult.result.changes` are empty); read the plan for them. It keeps `applyResult.staleUnits`, `.stalePaths` and every diagnostic, so it can be large; the `job.completed` event is a summary for that reason. Judge a finished job by `planResult.outcome` or `applyResult.outcome`, not by `state`.

state.description: `succeeded` whenever the run completed, whatever its outcome (see `JobState`).

RealtimeModelChanged.description: `model.changed` to every connection: the engine's ChangeSet (cut to 200 KB, `truncated` then true). With E5d each `ElementChange` carries the element's new `summary`, so the editor patches its index in place (and removes the rows of `deleted`); a change without a summary (an older server) or a truncated set makes it refetch `GET /api/model/index` with `If-None-Match`.

translations.description: After a translation change (reference-types-seeds-localization.md section 3.8): for each declared locale whose fallback chain includes a changed locale, the effective display names that changed (the fallback text when a translation was removed). Left out when none changed. Other fields are not sent: an open inspector or translation queue refetches its entries.

translationsTruncated.description: `translations` was dropped to fit 200 KB; the editor refetches the index for its content locale.

RealtimeValidationCompleted.description: `validation.completed` to every connection: a whole-model ValidationReport (cut to 200 KB; counts stay whole). The editor replaces its problems list with it, or refetches when `truncated`.

RealtimeProjectChanged.description: `project.changed` to every connection: settings, packs or extension schemas changed; refetch `GET /api/project` and the settings, and drop cached database views and previews (conventions and type maps change every resolved table). A `validation.completed` follows.

RealtimeTemplatesChanged.description: `templates.changed` to every connection: files of one pack changed on disk or through the API. Reload those files (a null hash means the file is gone); an empty `files` means reload the whole pack.

hash.description: The file's SHA-256 now, or null when it is gone or unknown.

RealtimePacksChanged.description: `packs.changed` to every connection: the packs whose files changed; refetch those packs (`GET /api/packs/{pack}`).

RealtimeJobProgress.description: `job.progress` to `job:{id}`: the running JobInfo with its latest `progress`, at most four per second.

RealtimeJobCompleted.description: `job.completed` to `job:{id}`: a fixed-size summary of the finished job (`JobCompletedEvent` in the functions), never the JobInfo. A finished JobInfo keeps `applyResult.staleUnits`, `.stalePaths`, `plan.request` and every diagnostic, which at S13 scale runs to megabytes, and the hub refuses payloads above 256 KB. On this event the editor reads `GET /api/jobs/{id}` and, for a plan job, `GET /api/generate/plan/{planId}`.

state.description: `succeeded` whenever the run completed, whatever its outcome (see `JobState`).

outcome.description: `planResult.outcome` or `applyResult.outcome`; `null` when the job ended without a result (cancelled before it ran, or an internal failure). What the editor reports.

planId.description: The plan a plan job produced; `null` for an apply job or a plan job without a plan.

error.description: The error of a failed job, cut to 2,000 characters.

JobCounts.description: Sizes of the lists a finished job holds, counted from the full record before the engine trims it.

changes.description: File decisions in the plan (plan job) or the run result (apply job).

errors.description: Error diagnostics of the plan or the run result.

RealtimePresenceChanged.description: `presence.changed` to `editors`: every live editor connection and its selection.

RealtimeSiteDeployed.description: `site.deployed`, sent by the host to every page after a deploy, rollback or functions upload went live.

enum.description: A closed set of named members.
